question: What is the overall length of Golden Quadrilateral in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**5846 km**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The overall length of the Golden Quadrilateral in India is **5846 km**.
 
• The Golden Quadrilateral is a highway network connecting India's four major metropolitan cities: Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata.
 
• This project was launched by the Government of India under the National Highways Development Project (NHDP).
 
• The objective of the Golden Quadrilateral is to improve road connectivity and facilitate faster movement of goods and people across the country.
 
• The project has significantly reduced travel time between these major cities and has boosted economic activities along the route.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Golden Quadrilateral project was initiated in 2001 and completed in 2012.
 
• It is one of the largest highway projects in the world and has played a pivotal role in improving the infrastructure and economy of India.
 
• The project was executed by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI).
 
• The Golden Quadrilateral forms a quadrilateral connecting the four major economic hubs of India, facilitating efficient transportation and trade.
 
• This highway network also connects several important industrial, agricultural, and cultural regions of India, making it a crucial infrastructure project for the nation.
